title: How Much Does a Dentist Cost in Barcelona? 2026 Price Guide
description: Typical 2026 dentist prices in Barcelona and Spain for check-ups, fillings, crowns and implants, plus how to find an English-speaking dentist.
excerpt: Dentistry in Spain is private and usually cheaper than in the UK or US. Here are the typical 2026 price ranges and how to avoid surprises.
tldr: In 2026 a typical dentist in Barcelona charges roughly €50 to €150 for a filling, €300 to €800 for a crown and €800 to €1,800 for a single implant, and routine dental care is private, not covered by the public system. Prices below are ranges from published clinic and comparison sources, so always ask for a written quote.

segments.text: Dental care in Spain is mostly private. The public health system covers little beyond emergencies, extractions and some children's care, so most residents and expats pay a private dentist directly or use an insurance plan. That is why prices vary so much between clinics, and why a written quote matters more than any average.

content.text: How much does a dentist cost in Barcelona in 2026?

segments.text: Barcelona dentists generally charge within the ranges below in 2026. Published sources agree on the shape of the pricing but not the exact figures, so treat these as guides and not as offers. Clinics in central and upmarket districts often charge somewhat more than clinics in smaller towns, with comparison sites putting the city premium at around 15 to 20 per cent.

items: Check-up (revisión): roughly €50 to €100, and many clinics offer a first visit free or at a reduced price.
Filling (empaste): roughly €50 to €150 per tooth, depending on size and material.
Tooth extraction: roughly €80 to €200, more for wisdom teeth or surgical removal.
Root canal (endodoncia): roughly €200 to €400 per tooth, and higher for molars.
Crown (corona): roughly €300 to €800, with metal-ceramic at the low end and zirconia at the high end.
Single dental implant: roughly €800 to €1,800 for the implant alone, and around €1,200 to €1,800 or more all-inclusive with crown.

content.text: Is dental work really cheaper in Spain than in the UK or US?

segments.text: Usually yes. Comparison sources suggest common treatments cost around 30 to 50 per cent less than in the UK or US, though that depends on the clinic and the treatment. Cheaper does not automatically mean lower quality, because Spanish dentists are university-trained and regulated. It does mean you should compare what is included, not just the headline price.

content.text: Does the public system or insurance cover dental care?

segments.text: Routine and cosmetic dental treatment is generally not covered by the Spanish public system, and Catalonia's public dental cover is limited, so most adults pay privately. Private health insurance in Spain often includes a basic dental package with discounted or free check-ups and cleanings, and some plans reimburse part of fillings or extractions. content.text: How do I find an English-speaking dentist in Barcelona?

segments.text: Start with clinics that say they offer treatment in English on their own website, and confirm by phone that the dentist, not just the receptionist, speaks English. Language matters most for treatment plans, consent forms and aftercare instructions, where a misunderstanding is expensive. Many Barcelona clinics run English versions of their sites, and some are set up specifically for international patients.

content.text: What should be in a dental quote?

segments.text: A good quote is written, itemised and dated. Before you agree to treatment, check the following:

items: Each procedure listed separately, tooth by tooth, with the price of each.
The materials used, for example the type of crown or the implant brand.
Whether X-rays, the first consultation and follow-up visits are included.
Whether the quote covers the whole treatment plan or only the first stage.
Payment terms: deposits, instalments and what happens if you stop midway.
The warranty on implants and crowns, and what it excludes.

content.text: Why do implant prices vary so much?

segments.text: Implant prices range widely because the figure quoted often covers different things. Some clinics advertise only the titanium post, while others price the post, the connector and the crown together. Bone grafts, sinus lifts, CT scans and temporary teeth can add to the total. Ask for the all-in price for the finished tooth, and ask what happens if you need extra bone work.

content.text: Do I need to worry about very cheap offers?

segments.text: Be cautious with promotional prices that look far below the ranges above. Some are genuine introductory offers, while others exclude the essential parts of the treatment or push you towards a bigger plan. Ask what the offer includes, get it in writing, and take time to compare a second quote before committing to major work.

content.text: How to keep dental costs down

items: Book regular check-ups so problems are caught while a filling is still enough.
Ask about clinic membership plans or annual hygiene packages.
Check whether your health insurance includes dental discounts.
Get two written quotes for any treatment above a few hundred euros.
Ask whether payment in instalments carries interest.

faqs.q: How much does a dentist cost in Barcelona?
faqs.a: In 2026 a check-up typically costs around €50 to €100, a filling €50 to €150, a crown €300 to €800 and a single implant €800 to €1,800. Prices vary by clinic, so ask for a written quote.

faqs.q: Is dental work cheaper in Spain?
faqs.a: Usually yes. Comparison sources put common treatments around 30 to 50 per cent below UK and US prices, though the difference depends on the clinic and the treatment.

faqs.q: Does Spanish public healthcare cover dentists?
faqs.a: Only in a limited way. Routine and cosmetic dental care is mostly private in Spain, so most adults pay directly or use private insurance with a dental package.

faqs.q: How do I find an English-speaking dentist in Barcelona?
faqs.a: Look for clinics that offer treatment in English on their own site, and confirm by phone that the dentist speaks English. Our Barcelona dentist directory lists English-speaking options by area.

faqs.q: How much is a dental implant in Barcelona?
faqs.a: Roughly €800 to €1,800 for the implant itself, and around €1,200 to €1,800 or more all-inclusive with the crown. Bone grafts and scans can add to the total.
